bootstrap.scheme: authors resampled with replacement within cohort; all sampled novels of a drawn author kept; 95% percentile interval

limits.sampling_bias: Project Gutenberg holds what volunteers digitised and what is out of U.S. copyright: it over-represents popular, canonical and genre fiction by British and American authors, and under-represents women, authors of colour and later cohorts whose works remain in copyright; c6 (born 1880-1899) is limited to works published before the U.S. public-domain cutoff, so its members are mostly early-career or early-publishing works. Cohort is birth-year based, so cohorts overlap in publication years (a c1 author writing in 1840 and a c3 author in 1850). Counts describe these (about) 120 novels, not the English novel; they show word use, not meaning, reception or cause.
limits.frame: The frame is the 320 most popular catalogue rows per cohort search (popularity-sorted by download count), so it favours books that are popular on Project Gutenberg today, not a random draw of the cohort's novels. Word counts are known only after the texts are loaded, so the 30,000-token rule is applied after loading and may shrink a cohort below 20 novels; then all cohorts are cut to the smallest n, as planned. Books with a translator in the catalogue record are excluded. The time axis is the author's birth year; no publication year is used.
limits.interpretation: descriptive patterns of word counts in 84 popular, digitised novels; cohort is birth-year based and overlaps in publication years; no causal claim
